about: Every Garmin Connect endpoint known to cyberjunky/python-garminconnect, plus the routes this plugin found in Garmin's own app and web traffic ("source": "plugin"), and what the plugin does with each one. Request shapes of upstream entries are generated; the `plugin`, `groups`, `cadence`, `check`, `critical`, `reads`, `schema` and `notes` keys are hand-written and survive regeneration. See api/README.md.

hosts.domain: garmin.com, or garmin.cn for China accounts

legend.path: Template. `{name}` is a path parameter; `{displayName}` is the URL-encoded social-profile display name.
legend.tier: Which host the path hangs off.
legend.plugin: The method in src/garmin/endpoints.ts that calls it, or absent if the plugin does not.
legend.groups: Metric groups (src/sync/metrics.ts) whose sync needs this endpoint.
legend.cadence: session = once per sign-in, day = one call per synced day, range = one call per window, paged = paged through, view = when a page opens, then cached in the vault.
legend.check: Covered by the daily contract check (.github/workflows/api-contract.yml).
legend.critical: Response paths the plugin reads. `[]` descends into array items. Losing one fails the check.
legend.schema: Recorded response shape, relative to api/.
legend.status: gone-upstream = present in an earlier catalogue, no longer in python-garminconnect.
legend.reads: Response paths the plugin reads but tolerates missing — a property that will not appear rather than a sync that breaks. Reported by the daily check, never fatal.
legend.graphql: POST /graphql-gateway/graphql entries only: the query's root field, which tells entries on that one path apart (scripts/garmin-web/summarize.mjs matches captured calls on it).

upstream.summary: The range form of get_endurance_score (startdate and enddate); verified through the plugin's client 2026-10-11.

endpoints.notes: aggregation=daily|weekly|monthly, 401 days a call at most for all three (402 is HTTP 400). groupMap: daily a key for every calendar day ({groupAverage = groupMax = the day's score, enduranceContributorDTOList = the day's list}, null/[] without data); weekly one group per Monday week touching the window, keyed by its Monday even before the start (the account's week start is ignored); monthly one per calendar month keyed by the 1st. groupAverage = floor(mean of the window's scored days in the group); groupMax = their max; contributions = mean of the daily shares over the window's days in the group that have a list (calibrating days count as group 8 at 100). avg = floor(mean of the non-null groupAverages); max = the highest day. enduranceScoreDTO = the newest scored day ≤ endDate, null when none. The endurance-score index walks it daily. The recorded schema comes from weekly and monthly samples only: the daily form keys every calendar day, so each date would be a field.

No parameters = daily + LATEST, every sport; sport is case-insensitive. weekly = 7-day blocks counted back from {end} (Monday weeks only when {end} is a Sunday; 2025-10-15..2026-10-14 gives Thursday–Wednesday rows), the block's last row per sport; monthly = calendar months. Cap end − start ≤ 366 days: 366 and 367 calendar days → 200, 368 → HTTP 400, also across Feb 29 (2023-10-11..2024-10-11 → 200 [], 2023-10-10..2024-10-11 → 400). An empty window → []. History from 2025-08-02 (35 dates, 46 rows to 2026-10-11); no row revised between 2026-10-11 22:29 and 2026-10-12 13:50. The FTP page's index asks daily without a sport.

The range form of get_hill_score (startdate and enddate), which upstream sends with aggregation=daily; weekly and monthly observed in connect.garmin.com web traffic, 2026-10-11 (ref/performance-stats/web-survey.md).

endpoints.notes: {userProfilePK, startDate, endDate, periodAvgScore, maxScore, hillScoreDTOList}. 401 days a call at most, whatever the aggregation (402 is HTTP 400). hillScoreDTOList: the days, newest first, rows as hill-score's, with daily and weekly aggregation alike (weekly 2026-07-20..10-11 sent 84), null with monthly, [] before the history. Days before the first row are left out, and today until the watch has scored it; every day from the first has a row, the first two weeks calibrating (no scores, hillScoreClassificationId 0, hillScoreFeedbackPhraseId 1). periodAvgScore is floor(mean of the scored days) per period, counting only the window's days: daily one key (the first row's date), weekly one per Monday week touching the window, keyed by its Monday even before the start (the account's week start is ignored), monthly keyed by each month's 1st; null for a period without a score. maxScore is the best day, null without one. vo2Max and vo2MaxPreciseValue are always null in the list. periodAvgScore is keyed by date, so the daily check sees new keys.

The summary equals the night's hrv-data-range row. lastNight5MinHigh = the top reading. Times: use the ...Local fields. The day sync keeps a night with readings in its series file (extra.hrvDay) and the HRV Status 1d page loads one on view.

upstream.summary: Return HRV (Heart Rate Variability) data for a date range.

endpoints.notes: {hrvSummaries, userProfilePk}, a night a row in ms, oldest first; nights without data are left out and a span with none is HTTP 204 (null). 367 days a call at most (368 is HTTP 400, re-verified 2026-10-12). History from 2025-08-03. status NONE: ONBOARDING_1 (first 18 nights, baseline null, weeklyAvg from night 4) or ONBOARDING_2 (after gaps: weeklyAvg and markerValue null). lastNightAvg/lastNight5MinHigh can be null with weeklyAvg and status present. markerValue = (weeklyAvg - (balancedLow - D/2)) / (2D), D = balancedUpper - balancedLow, when weeklyAvg >= balancedLow; another mapping below. Rows can appear up to 26 days after their night. The HRV Status page's index (hrv-status) reads it.

endpoints.notes: Keyed by the numeric profile id (socialProfile's profileId, which the plugin keeps from the display name lookup) rather than the display name. [] on the recording account for every window, the whole history included (no HRV stress test: it needs a chest strap; userstats availability lists ACTIVITY_HRV_STRESS_TEST as unavailable), so a row's shape is unknown and no schema can be recorded (api:record-file drops [] samples). No cap: 7, 28, 367, 368, 731, 3660 and 9,781 days (2000-01-01..2026-10-11) → 200 []. A reversed window → HTTP 500, which the client retries as transient, so GarminApi.hrvStressDaily refuses start > end. The web report (id 65, chartconfig ACTIVITY_HRV_STRESS_TEST, BAR_DAILY, 7D/30D) asks 7 days and a Sunday-aligned 4-week block; the plugin's HRV Stress index asks 3660-day windows.
